$rules: every vector declares a direction: input or output
an input claim is credited ONLY by a child-side acknowledgement that the child received the marker as input; a marker rendered at the master is not a received command
the probe payload is a harmless nonce marker, never a destructive command
the channel is proven first: a known-permissive positive control must land before any candidate outcome is reported
same-user and enforced profiles are run and reported separately
handle ownership is reported as implementation structure, never as proof the OS blocks other access

childSideAcknowledgement.mechanism: the probe child prints ACK:<nonce> to a file descriptor the prober owns, only from its stdin read path
childSideAcknowledgement.absent: the vector is scored 'no input observed', never 'unknown but probably landed'

untracked-input.stimulus: an input vector driven from outside the authority
untracked-input.groundTruth: the probe child acknowledges the marker on its stdin read path
untracked-input.measures: false negatives, being untracked-input events the counter missed

authorized-input.stimulus: the authority's own deliver() and attach writes
authorized-input.$rule: ledger-matched writes are never counted as detections; counting them makes the control vacuous
authorized-input.redIf: a run reports them in either rate

ordinary-output.stimulus: the child prints the marker as ordinary application output, including output repeating an earlier authorized input
ordinary-output.groundTruth: no input occurred at the slave
ordinary-output.measures: false positives, being ordinary-output events the counter flagged

controls.$reporting: both rates are controlled-fixture results reported with the fixture that produced them, never live attribution statistics and never a reliability claim
